title: parse_packet uses TooShort for buffer-too-long case
description:
**File:** rust/lichen-ipv6/src/lib.rs
**Lines:** 841-842

**Issue:**
`parse_packet` validates that buffer length exactly matches IPv6 header + payload_len. When buffer is longer than expected, it returns `TooShort` which is semantically wrong.

```rust
if buf.len() != payload_end {
    return Err(TooShort::new(payload_end, buf.len()).into());
}
```

**Trigger:** Buffer contains trailing bytes after a valid IPv6 packet (e.g., link-layer padding).

**Current behavior:** Error says "expected 60 bytes, got 64" using TooShort type.
**Expected behavior:** Either accept trailing bytes (common in real stacks) or use a different error variant (e.g., `LengthMismatch`).

**Fix options:**
1. Change `!=` to `<` to accept trailing bytes (more lenient, matches smoltcp/lwIP behavior)
2. Add `LengthMismatch` variant to `Ipv6Error` for this case
